title: Baseline: repetition code decoded from the first copy (33 ops)

claims.statement: Let f: {0,1}^1000 -> {0,1}^2000 be f(u) = (u, u) (each message bit sent twice) and let g(y) = (y_1, ..., y_1000). On a memoryless BSC with crossover probability 1/10 and a uniform message, the average block error probability satisfies eps(f, g) = 1 - (9/10)^1000 <= (10^46 - 1)/10^46.

For the same code and decoder (f(u) = (u, u), g(y) = (y_1, ..., y_1000)), implemented as the 33-instruction straight-line program in proof.md, g uses at most W = 33 <= 2^(101/20) operations in the bsc-ops-v1 model on every received word y in {0,1}^2000.

experiments.purpose: Check 9^1000 * 10^46 >= 10^1000 with exact integers, which is equivalent to (9/10)^1000 >= 10^-46.

Run the decoder program on the bsc-ops-v1 reference counter (byte-identical copy of reference/opmodel.py) on the all-zero, all-one and seeded random received words; report the op counts, that the output equals the first copy, and the exact check 33^20 <= 2^101.
